title: Company Insights: Know the company behind every candidate | Jack & Jill
markdown:
[Skip to main content](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights#main-content) Back to top

A candidate’s job title and past employers only tell you so much.

Have they worked at your stage? What did their team go through? Does a short stint warrant concern, or did they leave when lots of others did?

Your team needs that context to build a search and assess the people they find. But getting it means piecing together headcount, funding announcements and individual profiles. Without it, familiar company names can become a shortcut for relevant experience.

Today we’re launching Company Insights in Jill, putting that context alongside the candidate. Here’s how it can help your team.

## [Agree on what relevant experience looks like](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#agree-on-what-relevant-experience-looks-like)

“Startup experience” can mean a lot of things. See how early someone joined, company size when they joined and left, and funding raised during their stint.

![Their time here: an AI/ML engineer who joined in April 2025 as about employee #2,000. The company grew from 1,761 to 4,226 people and raised a Series G and Series H while they were there. They have been there 1.6 years, longer than 74% of people who have worked there](https://www.jackandjill.ai/images/resources/company-insights/their-time.webp)

That helps you get specific with your hiring manager: “someone who joined before 200 people and stayed through the next phase of growth.”

## [Assess whether they’ve seen your stage](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#assess-whether-theyve-seen-your-stage)

Explore how the business and the relevant team changed while a candidate was there. Use that context to ask about the challenges they handled and the part they played.

![A company profile filtered to sales: about 110 people, up 144% on the year before, with most hires coming from Amazon Web Services](https://www.jackandjill.ai/images/resources/company-insights/function.webp)

## [Put short stints in context](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#put-short-stints-in-context)

Compare their tenure with others and see whether they left during a wider wave of departures. Go into the conversation better informed about why they may have moved.

## [Expand your search](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#expand-your-search)

See where companies you admire hire from and where their people go next. Give your team more places to find relevant candidates, beyond the company names already in the brief.

![Talent flow: the eight companies most hires joined from and the eight most leavers went to, with eight engineers who left for Linear together](https://www.jackandjill.ai/images/resources/company-insights/talent-flow.webp)An illustrative example

## [Inform your hiring strategy](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#inform-your-hiring-strategy)

Explore which functions competitors are hiring into, where they find people and how long their hires stay. Use that evidence in conversations about your own hiring priorities and retention.

![Team insights: hiring by function against the current team, retention from six months to three years, locations and schools](https://www.jackandjill.ai/images/resources/company-insights/team.webp)An illustrative example

Company Insights gives your team a head start on the research, from the first conversation with a hiring manager to the candidates you put forward.

Open a candidate’s profile in Jill and click a company in their experience to explore.

## [Hire remarkable candidates who’d never apply.](https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/company-insights\#hire-remarkable-candidates-whod-never-apply)

Tell Jill who you need. She helps sharpen the brief, brings you a focused shortlist from Jack’s network, and introduces you directly when there’s a fit, including people who aren’t actively looking.
